= testdata

Test resources (XML, JSON, CJ, …) plus a ClassGraph-based loader (`TestFileProvider`,
`TestFileUtil`) used as a test-scoped dependency by the reader/writer modules.

== External test data (graph-test-data)

Bulky and shared datasets are being migrated out of this module into the external
https://github.com/Calpano/graph-test-data[graph-test-data] repository, which mirrors the same
top-level layout (`xml/`, `json/`, `text/`, `binary/`). This keeps the published `testdata` artifact
small (Maven Central limits, see `doc/maven-central.adoc`) and lets the data be shared across projects.

`TestFileProvider` treats the external checkout as an *additional* resource root: its files are merged
into every provider (`graphmlResources()`, `xmlResources()`, `cjResources*()`, …) and into
`--EXPECTED` lookups, deduplicated by path (the external copy wins on collision).

[IMPORTANT]
====
As migration has progressed, the external checkout is now *required* to run the full test suite.
Several tests load migrated files by exact path (e.g. `XmlTest.testNamespaces`,
`GraphmlReaderTest2`, `GioEngineCoreTest`) and will *fail* — not skip — without it.
Parameterized providers still degrade gracefully (fewer cases), but the build as a whole needs the
data repo checked out.
====

=== Enabling it

Check out the data repo and point the loader at it, in this resolution order:

. System property: `mvn test -Dgraph.test.data.dir=/path/to/graph-test-data`
. Environment variable: `export GRAPH_TEST_DATA_DIR=/path/to/graph-test-data`
. Auto-discovery: a sibling directory `../graph-test-data` or `../../graph-test-data` of the project.

[NOTE]
====
Surefire forks a separate JVM for tests. The forked JVM inherits *environment variables*
automatically, but *not* `-D` system properties. So `GRAPH_TEST_DATA_DIR` (env) works out of the box,
while `-Dgraph.test.data.dir` works because the loader is read in-process during classpath scanning.
For CI, prefer the environment variable.
====

To verify the external data is active, run a parameterized GraphML test with and without the root and
compare the case count — the difference equals the number of migrated files:

[source,bash]
----
mvn -pl reader-graphml test -Dtest=GraphmlTest                                   # in-repo only
GRAPH_TEST_DATA_DIR=/path/to/graph-test-data mvn -pl reader-graphml test -Dtest=GraphmlTest
----

=== CI

`.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml` checks out `graph-test-data` as a sibling of the project and
exports `GRAPH_TEST_DATA_DIR` for the build step.

== File-name tag convention (`--TAG`)

Test files carry semantics in their name via a double-dash tag, inserted before the extension(s):
`name--TAG.ext` (multi-dot extensions are preserved, e.g. `dingo--EXPECTED.graphml.xml`). A tag written
without a hyphen is upper-cased automatically. This is implemented in `TestFileUtil`
(`tagResourcePath`, `tagFile`, `tags`, constant `EXPECTED`) — that class is the authoritative source.

[cols="1,1,3", options="header"]
|===
| Tag | Read by code? | Meaning

| `--EXPECTED`
| Yes
| The recorded expected output for a round-trip/serialization test. Stored as
  `name--EXPECTED-<testId>.ext` and located/compared by `TestFileUtil.verifyOrRecord(...)` /
  `expectedResource(...)`. Such files are excluded from the normal input streams
  (`getAllTestResources()` filters `isExpected()`). Use env `RECORD_MODE=init\|on` to (re)record them.

| `--INVALID`
| Yes
| Marks input that is intentionally malformed, used to test error handling. Detected by
  `TestFileUtil.isInvalid(Resource, markers...)`, which inspects the `--` tag. The optional suffix
  qualifies *how* it is invalid: `--INVALIDxml` (not even well-formed XML),
  `--INVALIDgraphml` (valid XML but invalid GraphML), or bare `--INVALID`. Example
  `root--INVALIDgraphml.graphml`; see the _File naming_ section of the
  https://github.com/Calpano/graph-test-data[graph-test-data] README.

| `--FIXED`
| No
| Human convention only — a manually corrected, valid counterpart of a sibling `--INVALID`/broken file
  (e.g. `greek2--FIXED.graphml`). No code reads this tag; it is documentation for maintainers.
|===

== Metadata convention

The external repo documents data provenance with `meta.ddot` files (https://ddot.it[ddot.it] triples:
source URL, download date, license), superseding the older in-repo `info.meta` (`url-info=`) files.
